title: Inside the $2 Billion Side Hustle Paying People to Eat Out & Drive Around
promo_conflict: Mercedes promotes her iShop training and recruiting organization and ShopQuest; its performance and shopper earnings claims are not independently verified.

stated_problem.quote: They want to know what's going on from a customer's point of view.
stated_problem.speaker: Mercedes

idea.name: Mystery shopping
idea.one_liner: Shoppers evaluate businesses as customers and submit reports; providers pay them per assignment and may reimburse required purchases.
idea.customer: Businesses seeking customer-experience feedback, usually through mystery-shopping providers.
idea.offer: Visit or assess a location or website as a customer, then report on the experience.
idea.revenue_model: Per-shop fees, sometimes with reimbursement for required purchases; not hourly pay.

key_quotes.quote: We deliver insight from a real customer's point of view.
I've been mystery shopping personally for over 13 years.
So route shopping is where you're piecing together multiple mystery shops in one route.
I think my personal best in one day, $600 in one day.

claims.claim: The host says mystery shoppers average $500 a week on the side.
claims.quote: They average between $500 a week just doing this on the side.

claims.claim: A shopper earned $850 in less than two days.
claims.quote: She made $850 in less than two days.

claims.claim: A shopper earns over six figures a year from full-time mystery shopping.
claims.quote: I know a shopper who he makes over six figures a year.

claims.claim: A shopper earned over $65,000 in 2025.
claims.quote: One of our shoppers, she did 65,000 and some change in 2025.

claims.claim: There are thousands of mystery shops, especially across the US.
claims.quote: There are thousands and thousands of shops, especially across the US.

claims.claim: Mercedes says she has personally mystery shopped for over 13 years.
claims.quote: I've been mystery shopping personally for over 13 years.

claims.claim: Company data is described as showing side shoppers average between $2 and $500 a week, as transcribed.
claims.quote: They average between $2 and $500 a week, just doing this on the side.

claims.claim: A shopper can make $200 in a day by route shopping.
claims.quote: So $200 can be made in one day, you know, if you're route shopping.

claims.claim: Mercedes's personal best was $600 in one day.
claims.quote: I think my personal best in one day, $600 in one day.

claims.claim: A shopper may reach $2 to $500 a week by going out one or two days a week, as transcribed.
claims.quote: So even if you're doing this as a side hustle, maybe just going out one or two days a week, you can still hit that, you know, $2 to $500 a week.

claims.claim: A shopper could string together five shops in a route.
claims.quote: I'm gonna pick a day and then I am going to string together, let's say five mystery shops.

claims.claim: Mercedes used to spend one day a month doing about 20 car-wash shops.
claims.quote: So I can just tell you every month, I would take one day a month and I would go out and get my car washed about 20 times.

claims.claim: That car-wash route earned Mercedes $600.
claims.quote: And literally would make $600 and be back in time for dinner at my house with my kids.

claims.claim: A report for the car-wash shops usually took Mercedes under 15 minutes.
claims.quote: and then the report usually would take me under 15 minutes to do.

claims.claim: Mercedes describes mystery shopping as a $2 billion industry.
claims.quote: As the mystery shopping industry's like a $2 billion industry, right?

claims.claim: A provider may prevent a shopper from repeating a shop for another 30 days.
claims.quote: there might be a shop that you do this month that they say, okay, you can't do this for another 30 days.

claims.claim: A company vice president told Mercedes they needed 35, 40,000 shops a month, as transcribed.
claims.quote: he's like, man, we really 35, 40,000 shops a month.

claims.claim: Mercedes gives a lower average estimate of $25 to $40 per hour.
claims.quote: I'll give you a lower average, 25 to 40.

claims.claim: Mercedes says one website shop took 30 minutes and paid $300.
claims.quote: All I had to do was go onto a website and take screenshots of like walking through the process of this website, 30 minutes, $300.

acquisition_channels.details: Sign up with mystery-shopping providers individually and browse their websites for assignments.
Organizations connect shoppers with partner providers; good work can also lead to word of mouth between providers.
Shoppers can network with provider representatives at mystery-shopping conferences.

ideas.delivery: The shopper visits or evaluates a business or website, follows the assignment, and submits a report; the provider contracts and pays the shopper, with reimbursement for some required purchases.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act may apply if reports or photos capture identifiable employees or customers. Shoppers should account for UK self-employment tax rules.

stated_problem.quote: a lot of people don't know about it, don't know how to get started
stated_problem.speaker: Mercedes

idea.name: iShop mystery-shopper training and recruiting
idea.one_liner: An organization recruits and trains mystery shoppers, connects them with legitimate providers, and offers continued support.
idea.customer: People looking to start mystery shopping and providers seeking prepared shoppers.
idea.offer: Free and paid training, support, and introductions to partner mystery-shopping companies.
idea.revenue_model: Paid training; the price and any provider-side revenue are not stated.

key_quotes.quote: Like we recruit, we train shoppers, but yes.
So we are not the provider, but we are the recruiter.
We are the people that you go to to kind of have a safe home base as a mystery shopper.
So we have a free training, we have a paid training, and then we have continued support.

claims.claim: Mercedes says mystery-shopping organizations generally charge for training.
claims.quote: It's industry standard to pay for training. If you look at any mystery shopping organization, they all charge for training.

claims.claim: Some people say they earned six or seven dollars from mystery shopping without training.
claims.quote: I did mystery shopping and it was paying six and seven dollars.

claims.claim: Mercedes says people who report low earnings had not started through an organization in 100% of the cases she asked about.
claims.quote: And my first question is, did you start through an organization and 100% of the time it is no?

claims.claim: iShop offers both free and paid training, plus continued support.
claims.quote: So we have a free training, we have a paid training, and then we have continued support.

claims.claim: The host describes iShop as having thousands and thousands of members.
claims.quote: turning this eye shop into a pretty serious business at this point with thousands and thousands of members

claims.claim: A partner company told Mercedes that iShop shoppers filled four hard-to-reach areas.
claims.quote: I was able to fill four of our hard to reach areas with your shoppers

acquisition_channels.details: Mercedes says word of mouth brings in shoppers.
Social media and podcast interviews are used to spread the opportunity.
iShop connects with mystery-shopping providers and supplies trained shoppers.

ideas.delivery: The organization recruits shoppers, provides training and ongoing support, and connects them to provider companies. Mercedes describes delivery through an organization and its team.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to shopper profiles and personal data handled in reports. If operating in the UK as a work-finding intermediary, check the Employment Agencies Act and Conduct of Employment Agencies and Employment Businesses Regulations 2003. Paid training terms should be clear to consumers.

idea.name: Mystery-shopping conference
idea.one_liner: An in-person event for shoppers and provider companies to learn, network, and market themselves; how it earns money is not stated.
idea.customer: Mystery shoppers and mystery-shopping company representatives.
idea.offer: A conference with learning and networking opportunities.

key_quotes.quote: There are conferences, mystery shopping conferences and that's where you can actually get in front of them with your face in person.
Yeah, so there's only two. It's ours and the other organization.
Last year, we had over a hundred.
Our first conference was in 22.

claims.claim: Mercedes says there are two mystery-shopping conferences in the industry.
claims.quote: Yeah, so there's only two. It's ours and the other organization.

claims.claim: The conference had over 100 attendees the prior year.
claims.quote: Last year, we had over a hundred.

claims.claim: The first conference was held in 2022.
claims.quote: Our first conference was in 22.

claims.claim: Mercedes hopes for close to 200 attendees that year.
claims.quote: So hopefully this year, you know, we have closer to 200.

ideas.delivery: Organizers host an in-person conference attended by shoppers and provider companies; the cited year's event was planned for Las Vegas.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR may apply to attendee registration and marketing data if the event is run in the UK.

idea.name: Event photography
idea.one_liner: A photographer provides coverage for private events such as reunions; prices and business details are not stated.
idea.customer: Event organizers or private event hosts.

key_quotes.quote: my wife had one of these as a photographer
We're having a reunion, you know, this is the venue or you available

ideas.delivery: The photographer attends the event and takes photographs; no further delivery details are given.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR and privacy considerations may apply to storing or sharing identifiable event photographs.

idea.name: Retail merchandising shops
idea.one_liner: Workers visit retail stores to photograph or scan merchandise and sometimes place stickers, receiving pay through a merchandising assignment.
idea.customer: Retailers and merchandising providers that need in-store product checks.
idea.offer: Visit stores, scan aisles, take product photos, or place stickers.
idea.revenue_model: Assignment or hourly pay; amounts depend on the assignment.

key_quotes.quote: Merchandising, it's all about the merch.
It's taking pictures, it's putting stickers on products and things like that.
So you will see that when you are a mystery shopper.

claims.claim: The host describes a Hettle assignment to scan 10 aisles at Target.
claims.quote: go to Target and scan, you know, these 10 aisles

claims.claim: The host says one assignment involved about 65 aisles.
claims.quote: It took, one of them was like 65 aisles.

claims.claim: The host estimates that assignment took an hour and 45 minutes.
claims.quote: That probably took an hour, 45.

claims.claim: The host says the Hettle work paid about $20 an hour.
claims.quote: But worked out to, worked out to about 20 bucks an hour.

claims.claim: The host earlier estimates the same Hettle assignment at about $20 an hour.
claims.quote: And they ended up paying, you probably worked out to about 20 bucks an hour.

acquisition_channels.details: Assignments can be found through the Hettle app or merchandising work offered by mystery-shopping companies.

ideas.delivery: A worker goes into retail stores, scans or photographs merchandise, and may place stickers; providers or apps assign the work.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR may apply if store photos capture identifiable customers or staff.

idea.name: ShopQuest mystery-shop job aggregator
idea.one_liner: A free-to-join site lets shoppers browse mystery-shop jobs by area and is adding more features; monetization is not stated.
idea.offer: Aggregate and browse local mystery-shopping jobs, with route-related features in development.
idea.revenue_model: Free to join; other revenue is not stated.

key_quotes.quote: We launched it three months ago, and we're still adding features and things like that.
Yes, that is open to the public and you're able to kind of see shops in your area and start browsing, it's pretty cool.
There's thousands of shops on there right now.
unlock secret shopper jobs in your city, 100% free to join

claims.claim: Mercedes says ShopQuest launched three months before the interview and was still adding features.
claims.quote: We launched it three months ago, and we're still adding features and things like that.

claims.claim: Mercedes says ShopQuest had thousands of shops listed at the time.
claims.quote: There's thousands of shops on there right now.

claims.claim: The host reads a tagline saying ShopQuest is 100% free to join.

ideas.delivery: A website aggregates mystery-shop assignments for shoppers to browse by area; route-related tools were being built or added by the team.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to shopper profile data. If the service introduces UK work seekers to hirers or providers, check the Employment Agencies Act and Conduct of Employment Agencies and Employment Businesses Regulations 2003.

if you have now thousands of thousands of trained VA's, all of a sudden people wanting to hire those people will come to you and say, and now you can kind of be the matchmaker becomes even more valuable.
